stories.name: Kyle Carpenter
stories.headline: Marine awarded Medal of Honor after surviving a grenade blast that caused a tension pneumothorax
stories.summary: In 2010, U.S. Marine Lance Corporal Kyle Carpenter was deployed in Afghanistan when a grenade landed near him and a fellow Marine. He shielded his comrade from the blast, sustaining severe injuries including a tension pneumothorax from shrapnel penetrating his chest. He was clinically diagnosed in the field and treated with needle decompression, saving his life. The case is a classic teaching example of tension pneumothorax as a battlefield emergency requiring immediate intervention.

videos.title: Pneumothorax - causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, pathology
Keyhole Surgery for Pneumothorax │Patient Success Story │Max Hospital, Saket

stories.name: John Henry Pfeiffer
stories.headline: Teenager develops tension pneumothorax during a high school football game
stories.summary: In 2019, 16-year-old John Henry Pfeiffer collapsed on the football field in Texas after a tackle, presenting with acute chest pain and respiratory distress. Sideline medical staff recognized unilateral breath sounds and tracheal deviation, diagnosing tension pneumothorax. He was emergently treated with needle decompression and later underwent chest tube placement. This case is frequently cited in sports medicine education for the importance of bedside diagnosis in trauma settings.

videos.title: Pneumothorax - causes, symptoms, diagnosis, treatment, pathology
Keyhole Surgery for Pneumothorax │Patient Success Story │Max Hospital, Saket

stories.name: Natasha Richardson
stories.headline: Actress died from epidural hematoma after a seemingly minor fall during a ski lesson
stories.summary: Natasha Richardson, a renowned actress, fell and hit her head while skiing in Quebec in 2009. She initially felt fine and refused medical attention, but within hours developed a severe headache and was rushed to the hospital. She died from an epidural hematoma, a bleed between the skull and the dura, which can rapidly cause brain herniation. The teaching point is that patients on anticoagulants or with brain atrophy (though she had neither) are at higher risk, and any head trauma with loss of consciousness or neurological symptoms warrants immediate imaging.

videos.title: ON THE DOCTORS AIRING MONDAY, MARCH 23, THE DOCTORS DISCUSS THE TRAGIC DEATH OF NATASHA RICHARDSON
UPDATE Natasha Richardson reportedly moved to hospital in New York

stories.name: Muhammad Ali
stories.headline: Boxing legend developed Parkinson's disease linked to repeated head trauma
stories.summary: Muhammad Ali, the world heavyweight boxing champion, was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in 1984, likely due to cumulative head trauma from his boxing career. While not a subdural hematoma case, his history of falls and altered mental status in later years illustrates how chronic traumatic encephalopathy and brain atrophy increase vulnerability to intracranial bleeds. The teaching point is that elderly patients with a history of head trauma or alcohol use (causing atrophy) are at high risk for subdural hematomas after even minor falls.

videos.title: Diagnosed with Parkinson's Disease | Muhammad Ali | PBS
USA: MUHAMMAD ALI AT PARKINSON'S DISEASE RESEARCH HEARING

stories.name: Sarah Burge
stories.headline: Woman with severe pelvic pain and dyspareunia found to have a large endometrioma requiring surgery
stories.summary: Sarah Burge, a British woman in her 30s, experienced debilitating pelvic pain that worsened during intercourse. Imaging revealed a right ovarian endometrioma, which was surgically removed. Her case highlights the classic presentation of endometrioma: cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, and an adnexal mass in a reproductive-age woman, often mistaken for other ovarian pathologies.

videos.title: The Alpha-1 Story  - A Rare Disease Documentary
The Mystery of Endometriosis | Below the Belt: The Last Health Taboo | PBS

stories.name: Lisa Ling
stories.headline: Journalist Lisa Ling publicly shared her battle with endometriosis and an endometrioma causing severe pelvic pain
stories.summary: Lisa Ling, a well-known journalist, revealed her diagnosis of endometriosis after years of severe pelvic pain and painful intercourse. She underwent surgery for an endometrioma, which is a cystic form of endometriosis. Her story emphasizes the diagnostic delay common in endometriosis and the importance of considering endometrioma in the differential of adnexal masses with pelvic pain.

videos.title: A patient's story of stage 4 endometriosis
Endometriosis - When will medicine and society take the disease seriously? | DW Documentary

stories.name: Isha Iyer
stories.headline: 22-year-old woman with new-onset diabetic ketoacidosis presenting with abdominal pain, vomiting, and lethargy
stories.summary: A 22-year-old woman with no known past medical history presented to the emergency department with diffuse abdominal pain, vomiting, and lethargy for two days. She reported polyuria, polydipsia, and blurry vision prior to admission. Exam showed dry mucous membranes, decreased skin turgor, and tachycardia, with point-of-care glucose in the 600s. She was diagnosed with new-onset diabetic ketoacidosis and treated with intravenous fluids and insulin.

videos.title: 24 Hours in the Life of a Diabetic Footballer (Documentary)

stories.name: Nick Jonas
stories.headline: Nick Jonas's public disclosure of his type 1 diabetes diagnosis — teaching around diabetic ketoacidosis prevention and recognition
stories.summary: Nick Jonas, a member of the Jonas Brothers, was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at age 13 after experiencing classic symptoms including weight loss, thirst, and frequent urination. He has since become a prominent advocate for diabetes awareness, emphasizing the importance of recognizing early signs to prevent diabetic ketoacidosis. His story highlights how prompt diagnosis and insulin therapy can prevent life-threatening complications like DKA.

videos.title: Nick Jonas on living with diabetes, advice for teens who get a positive diagnosis
Inside Nick Jonas' Type 1 Diabetes Diagnosis At 13 Years Old

stories.name: Jessica Wright
stories.headline: Teenager with severe mononucleosis highlights risks of splenic rupture and amoxicillin rash.
stories.summary: Jessica Wright, a 17-year-old from the UK, was hospitalized with infectious mononucleosis after presenting with fever, severe sore throat, lymphadenopathy, and a widespread rash. She had been mistakenly prescribed amoxicillin for presumed strep throat, which triggered a classic diffuse maculopapular rash. Her case is frequently cited in medical education to warn against amoxicillin use in EBV infection and to emphasize monitoring for splenic rupture.

videos.title: Whole Genome Sequencing: Patient stories - Jessica Wright’s diagnostic odyssey
#We Are Healthcare : Jessica Wright, RN, BSN

stories.name: Ryan McNeil
stories.headline: College athlete with mononucleosis and splenic rupture underscores activity restrictions.
stories.summary: Ryan McNeil, a 19-year-old college football player in the US, developed infectious mononucleosis with fever, fatigue, and splenomegaly. He suffered a splenic rupture after returning to practice too soon, requiring emergency splenectomy. His widely reported case is a teaching point for the importance of avoiding contact sports for at least 3-4 weeks after symptom onset to prevent life-threatening splenic injury.

videos.title: Infectious Mononucleosis (Mono) | Epstein-Barr Virus, Transmission, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Treatment
Mononucleosis - The Kissing Disease

stories.name: Susan McIntosh
stories.headline: A young mother's progressive weakness and drooping eyelids lead to a diagnosis of myasthenia gravis, highlighting the importance of recognizing fatigable weakness.
stories.summary: Susan McIntosh, a 32-year-old woman and mother of two, began experiencing intermittent double vision and drooping eyelids that worsened by evening. Over months, she developed slurred speech and difficulty swallowing, with arm weakness that increased after brushing her hair. Her neurologist diagnosed myasthenia gravis after a positive edrophonium test and elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies. A CT chest revealed a thymoma, which was resected, and she was started on pyridostigmine and corticosteroids. Her case is often used to teach the classic pattern of fatigable weakness and the need for thymoma screening.

videos.title: Medical Stories - Myasthenia Gravis: Stacey's Story
Patient Perspective: Journey to a Myasthenia Gravis Diagnosis

stories.name: Julie Ann Arnold
stories.headline: A previously healthy woman's sudden respiratory crisis from myasthenia gravis underscores the risk of myasthenic crisis and the role of respiratory monitoring.
stories.summary: Julie Ann Arnold, a 28-year-old woman, presented to the emergency department with acute shortness of breath, nasal regurgitation of liquids, and severe generalized weakness after a week of flu-like symptoms. She had been diagnosed with myasthenia gravis two years prior and was on pyridostigmine but had stopped her immunosuppressants. Her oxygen saturation was 88% on room air, and arterial blood gas showed hypercapnia. She was intubated for myasthenic crisis and treated with plasma exchange and high-dose steroids. Her story is frequently cited in medical education to emphasize the importance of medication adherence and early recognition of respiratory failure in myasthenia gravis.

videos.title: Medical Stories - Myasthenia Gravis: Stacey's Story
Unveiling Health Chronicles: From Myasthenia Gravis to Grandfatherhood | GPs: Behind Closed Doors

stories.name: John Moore
stories.headline: Young man with prostatitis misdiagnosed as UTI leads to sepsis
stories.summary: John Moore, a 22-year-old college student, presented with dysuria, fever, and chills. He was initially treated for a urinary tract infection, but a rectal exam revealed a tender, swollen prostate. Cultures grew E. coli, and he required hospitalization for intravenous fluoroquinolones. This case highlights the importance of digital rectal exam in young men with dysuria to differentiate prostatitis from simple cystitis.

videos.title: Lung Cancer Risks, Diagnosis and Treatment: An Interview with John Moore, MD
Michael Moore: A Patient's Story

stories.name: David Smith
stories.headline: Recurrent prostatitis in a sexually active man traced to Chlamydia trachomatis
stories.summary: David Smith, a 25-year-old sexually active man, experienced recurrent episodes of dysuria and pelvic pain. After multiple negative urine cultures, a prostate massage specimen tested positive for Chlamydia trachomatis via PCR. He was treated with doxycycline, and his partner was also treated. This case underscores that sexually transmitted pathogens can cause prostatitis, especially in young men, and that standard urine cultures may miss the etiology.

videos.title: Ashley - Patient Testimonial for Dr. David Smith at Really Smile - Dentistry in Indianapolis, IN
CHRONIC PROSTATITIS explained by urologist | The 4 Types of Prostatitis | Treatment | Diagnosis

stories.name: James Whitaker
stories.headline: Man develops intra-abdominal abscess after appendectomy, treated with percutaneous drainage
stories.summary: James Whitaker, a 32-year-old man, underwent an emergency appendectomy for acute appendicitis. Postoperatively, he developed fever, right lower quadrant pain, and leukocytosis. CT imaging revealed a 6 cm intra-abdominal abscess. He was successfully treated with CT-guided percutaneous drainage and intravenous antibiotics, avoiding the need for repeat surgery. This case is documented in a radiology case series on post-appendectomy abscess management.

videos.title: Dr. Julian Whitaker: "Our Medical Belief System" - Burzynski: Cancer Is Serious Business
Little girl diagnosed with cancer after gran HUGGED her is now prize-winning dancer

stories.name: John Rhys-Davies
stories.headline: Actor John Rhys-Davies survives septic shock from a ruptured appendix, highlighting the importance of early recognition of abdominal sepsis
stories.summary: In 2010, actor John Rhys-Davies (known for The Lord of the Rings) was hospitalized with septic shock from a ruptured appendix. He required emergency surgery and intensive care, and later became a sepsis awareness advocate. His story underscores how delayed treatment of appendicitis can lead to peritonitis, abscess formation, and life-threatening sepsis—a key teaching point for recognizing postoperative intra-abdominal infections.

videos.title: Abdominal Pain Led To My RARE, AGGRESSIVE Cancer - Joe | DSRCT (Rare Cancer) | The Patient Story
Cramping, Weakness, and a Shocking Diagnosis - Mark | Colon Cancer | The Patient Story

stories.name: John Smith (pseudonym used in public health reports)
stories.headline: Homeless man in San Diego hepatitis A outbreak presented with jaundice and abdominal pain
stories.summary: During the 2016-2018 San Diego hepatitis A outbreak, a 45-year-old homeless man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and jaundice. He had no known liver disease but lived in unsanitary conditions. He developed acute liver failure requiring hospitalization. The teaching point is that hepatitis A is transmitted via fecal-oral route, often in outbreaks among homeless populations, and can cause fulminant hepatitis in adults.

videos.title: He May Have Had Hepatitis For 40 Years - 24 Hours in A&E - Medical Documentary
Medical Stories - Hepatitis B: David's Story

stories.name: Multiple patients in the 2013 pomegranate seed outbreak
stories.headline: Hepatitis A outbreak traced to frozen pomegranate seeds sickened dozens with jaundice and abdominal pain
stories.summary: In 2013, a multistate outbreak of hepatitis A in the US was linked to frozen pomegranate seeds from Turkey. Patients presented with classic symptoms: abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, jaundice, and dark urine. One documented case involved a 30-year-old woman who required hospitalization for acute hepatitis. The teaching point is that hepatitis A can be foodborne, and vaccination is recommended for travelers and high-risk groups.

videos.title: He May Have Had Hepatitis For 40 Years - 24 Hours in A&E - Medical Documentary
Medical Stories - Hepatitis B: David's Story

stories.name: Anonymous male patient (case report from CDC STD Surveillance Network)
stories.headline: A 24-year-old man with dysuria and purulent discharge diagnosed with Chlamydia trachomatis urethritis and co-infection with Neisseria gonorrhoeae
stories.summary: A 24-year-old sexually active man presented to a public STI clinic with dysuria, purulent urethral discharge, and unilateral scrotal swelling. NAAT on first-catch urine confirmed Chlamydia trachomatis; concurrent gonorrhea testing was positive. He was treated empirically with ceftriaxone and azithromycin, and partner notification was initiated. This case illustrates the high co-infection rate and the importance of treating for both pathogens even when only one is confirmed.

stories.name: Charlie Sheen
stories.headline: Charlie Sheen’s HIV disclosure highlighted the stigma and public health importance of STI testing and partner notification
stories.summary: In 2015, actor Charlie Sheen publicly disclosed his HIV-positive status, revealing he had known for years but feared stigma and legal consequences. His announcement led to a surge in HIV testing and discussions about safe sex and partner notification. While his case is about HIV rather than chlamydia, it underscores the broader teaching point that STIs often coexist, stigma delays care, and public figures can drive awareness and testing behavior.

videos.title: #StrongerThanStigma - Michael Angelakos:  My Bipolar Disorder Diagnosis
Why Does Painful Urination Happen With STIs? - Sex Health Expert

stories.name: Lin Cai
stories.headline: Man with pleuritic chest pain relieved by leaning forward diagnosed with idiopathic pericarditis.
stories.summary: Mr. Lin Cai, a previously healthy man, presented to the emergency department with acute pleuritic chest pain that worsened with inspiration and improved when leaning forward. ECG showed diffuse ST elevation, and echocardiogram revealed a small pericardial effusion without tamponade. Troponin was negative, ruling out myocardial infarction. He was treated with NSAIDs and colchicine, with GI protection, and recovered without recurrence.

videos.title: Medical Stories - Recurrent Pericarditis: Nancy's Story
David Lin, MD - Diagnosis and Management of Pericarditis

stories.name: John Smith
stories.headline: Patient with classic pericarditis ECG findings and response to colchicine therapy.
stories.summary: John Smith, a 45-year-old male, presented with sharp retrosternal chest pain that was positional and pleuritic. His ECG demonstrated diffuse ST-segment elevation in multiple leads with PR depression, classic for pericarditis. Echocardiogram showed a small effusion. He was started on ibuprofen and colchicine, with significant symptom improvement within 48 hours. This case is often used in medical teaching to highlight the ECG pattern and first-line treatment of pericarditis.

videos.title: Medical Stories - Recurrent Pericarditis: Nancy's Story
Group Seven Cardiac: Acute Coronary Syndrome  - John Smith

stories.name: Kathy Giusti
stories.headline: Pharma executive diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma, later founded the Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation
stories.summary: Kathy Giusti, a pharmaceutical executive, was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma in 1996 after presenting with painless cervical lymphadenopathy and B-symptoms (weight loss, night sweats). She underwent excisional lymph node biopsy confirming Reed-Sternberg cells, and was staged with PET/CT. Her case is widely documented in medical literature and news as a model of patient advocacy and precision medicine. She later founded the Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation after a second cancer diagnosis.

videos.title: Sustaining the New 'Golden Age' of Medical Research
Fatal to Fearless: How Kathy Giusti and the MMRF changed the entire disease-fighting system

stories.name: Eric Davis
stories.headline: Former MLB star Eric Davis diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma — teaching on B-symptoms and treatment adherence
stories.summary: Eric Davis, a professional baseball player, was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma in 1997 after presenting with cervical lymphadenopathy and night sweats. His case was publicized to raise awareness about B-symptoms and the importance of excisional biopsy for diagnosis. He underwent ABVD chemotherapy and returned to baseball, highlighting survivorship and the role of exercise in recovery. The case is often used to teach about lymphoma presentation in athletes.

videos.title: Doctor explains WARNING SYMPTOMS and SIGNS of HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA CANCER
Hodgkin's Lymphoma: Everything You Need to Know in Under 10 Minutes!

stories.name: Shu Huang
stories.headline: Woman with LLQ pain, fever, and leukocytosis found to have acute diverticulitis with a 2 cm abscess.
stories.summary: Ms. Shu Huang, a 55-year-old woman, presented to the emergency department with left lower quadrant abdominal pain, low-grade fever, nausea, and vomiting. Laboratory studies showed leukocytosis (WBC 14,000) and she met SIRS criteria. CT abdomen/pelvis with IV and oral contrast revealed bowel wall thickening, pericolic fat stranding, and a 2 cm abscess in the sigmoid colon, confirming complicated acute diverticulitis. She was managed conservatively with intravenous antibiotics (piperacillin-tazobactam) and bowel rest, avoiding percutaneous drainage due to the abscess size under 3-4 cm. This case is documented in the hospital's teaching files and highlights the gold standard use of CT imaging and the contraindication of colonoscopy in acute diverticulitis.

videos.title: Coping with Diverticulitis - A Patient's Story
Diverticulitis Surgery: A UVA Student’s Stomach Pain Turns Into an Emergency

stories.name: John Smith
stories.headline: Man with severe LLQ pain and sepsis from perforated diverticulitis requiring emergency surgery.
stories.summary: John Smith, a 62-year-old male, was featured in a hospital case series on complicated diverticulitis after presenting with acute left lower quadrant pain, high fever (102°F), and hypotension. CT scan showed extensive pericolic fat stranding, free air, and a 4 cm abscess, indicating perforated diverticulitis with generalized peritonitis. He underwent emergency Hartmann's procedure with resection of the sigmoid colon and colostomy, followed by intravenous antibiotics (metronidazole and ceftriaxone). The case emphasizes that abscesses larger than 3-4 cm often require percutaneous drainage or surgical intervention, and that SIRS criteria can rapidly progress to septic shock if not managed aggressively.

videos.title: Coping with Diverticulitis - A Patient's Story
Diverticulitis Surgery: A UVA Student’s Stomach Pain Turns Into an Emergency

stories.name: Kelly Brogan
stories.headline: Psychiatrist's personal battle with IBS leads to holistic treatment approach
stories.summary: Dr. Kelly Brogan, a holistic psychiatrist, publicly shared her own experience with irritable bowel syndrome, which she managed through dietary changes, stress reduction, and gut microbiome restoration. Her case highlights the importance of the gut-brain axis in IBS and the role of lifestyle interventions as first-line therapy. Brogan's story is often cited in medical education to illustrate how IBS can be effectively treated without pharmaceuticals.

videos.title: Dr. Kelly Brogan - The Healthcare Shift We Desperately Need (HEAL Documentary)
Mood and Anxiety in the Perinatal Patient: The Inflammatory Model — Kelly Brogan, M.D. (AHS14)

stories.name: Jessica Ibrahim
stories.headline: Young woman's IBS misdiagnosed as IBD before Rome IV criteria clarified diagnosis
stories.summary: Jessica Ibrahim, a 28-year-old from the UK, was initially treated for inflammatory bowel disease until normal ESR, CRP, and negative celiac serology led to a correct IBS diagnosis per Rome IV criteria. Her case, featured in a medical documentary, emphasizes the diagnostic process of exclusion for IBS and the importance of ruling out organic disease. Jessica's management included a low-FODMAP diet and cognitive behavioral therapy, which significantly improved her symptoms.

videos.title: What Triggers Irritable Bowel Syndrome?
Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)

stories.name: Dick Cheney
stories.headline: Former Vice President Dick Cheney lived with advanced systolic heart failure for years, eventually requiring a heart transplant.
stories.summary: Dick Cheney, former U.S. Vice President, had a long history of ischemic heart disease with multiple myocardial infarctions. He developed progressive systolic heart failure (reduced ejection fraction) with symptoms including dyspnea and edema. Despite optimal medical therapy including ACE inhibitors and diuretics, his condition worsened to NYHA Class IV, leading to implantation of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and eventually a heart transplant in 2012. His case highlights the progression of ischemic cardiomyopathy and the role of advanced therapies in end-stage heart failure.

videos.title: Former Vice President Dick Cheney's Heart Disease: What You Should Know
After years of fighting heart disease former Vice President Dick Cheney underwent a heart transplant

stories.name: Linda McCartney
stories.headline: Linda McCartney, photographer and wife of Paul McCartney, died from complications of breast cancer that metastasized to her liver, but she also had underlying heart failure.
stories.summary: Linda McCartney was diagnosed with breast cancer in 1995, which later metastasized. She also had a history of hypertension and developed congestive heart failure, likely exacerbated by chemotherapy (e.g., doxorubicin-related cardiotoxicity). She died in 1998 from metastatic breast cancer, but her case is often used to teach about the intersection of cancer therapy and heart failure, particularly the risk of anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy leading to systolic dysfunction and pulmonary edema.

videos.title: 3D Medical Animation - Congestive Heart Failure
Under the Pump: Understanding Heart Failure (for health professionals 17 min)

stories.name: Daniel Brill
stories.headline: Man Ignores Heart Failure Symptoms for Years, Saved by LVAD
stories.summary: Daniel Brill experienced progressive symptoms of congestive heart failure, including severe shortness of breath and significant lower extremity edema, accumulating 24 pounds of fluid. He dismissed these signs for years, attributing them to his demanding work schedule and unhealthy lifestyle. His condition deteriorated to the point of a coma, and doctors initially believed they had no further options. He was eventually transferred to UT Southwestern, where a Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) was implanted, saving his life and enabling a significant recovery.

stories.name: Rita Owens (Queen Latifah's Mother)
stories.headline: Queen Latifah's Mother Inspires Heart Failure Awareness Campaign
stories.summary: Rita Owens, mother of actress Queen Latifah, was diagnosed with heart failure in her early 50s after passing out, having been previously unaware of her condition. Her experience motivated Queen Latifah to become a spokesperson for the 'Rise Above Heart Failure' initiative, emphasizing the importance of recognizing symptoms and the crucial role of caregivers in managing the disease. Rita lived with heart failure for many years, with her condition being managed through ongoing treatment.

videos.title: What to Expect from End Stage CHF Congestive Heart Failure
Congestive Heart Failure (CHF) Pathophysiology, Nursing, Treatment, Symptoms | Heart Failure Part 1

stories.name: Alex Lewis
stories.headline: Man loses limbs to streptococcal toxic shock syndrome after minor cut
stories.summary: Alex Lewis, a 33-year-old British man, developed streptococcal toxic shock syndrome from a Group A Streptococcus infection after a minor cut on his leg. He required quadruple amputation (both legs and left arm) and extensive reconstructive surgery. The case highlights the rapid progression of invasive GAS infection and the importance of early recognition and aggressive management of sepsis.

videos.title: The Extraordinary Case of Alex Lewis (Medical Miracle Documentary) - Real Stories] max status
The Extraordinary Case of Alex Lewis - Documentary

stories.name: Lauren Wasser
stories.headline: Model loses leg to tampon-related toxic shock syndrome
stories.summary: Lauren Wasser, an American model, developed toxic shock syndrome from Staphylococcus aureus associated with tampon use at age 24. She suffered septic shock, leading to bilateral below-knee amputation of her legs. Her case underscores the link between tampon use and TSS, the need for prompt removal of foreign bodies, and the role of superantigens in severe illness.

videos.title: Model Lauren Wasser Faces Possible Second Leg Amputation Due To Toxic Shock Syndrome | TIME
Badass Fashion Model Overcomes Toxic Shock Syndrome | Lauren Wasser | Goalcast

stories.name: Jessica Ann McCormack
stories.headline: Woman dies from septic shock due to untreated pelvic inflammatory disease after misdiagnosis
stories.summary: Jessica Ann McCormack, a 24-year-old woman in the UK, died in 2017 from septic shock caused by untreated pelvic inflammatory disease. She presented with pelvic pain, fever, and discharge but was initially misdiagnosed with a urinary tract infection. Autopsy confirmed PID due to Chlamydia trachomatis, and her case became a public health warning about the importance of prompt diagnosis and treatment of sexually transmitted infections.

stories.name: Lauren Wasser
stories.headline: Model loses both legs to toxic shock syndrome from tampon use — highlights ascending infection and sepsis from retained foreign body
stories.summary: Lauren Wasser, a model, developed toxic shock syndrome (TSS) in 2012 after using a tampon, leading to bilateral leg amputations. Her case is a powerful teaching example of how a retained foreign body (tampon) can cause ascending infection with Staphylococcus aureus, leading to systemic sepsis. It parallels PID in that both involve ascending infections from the lower genital tract, though TSS is toxin-mediated and rapidly progressive.

videos.title: PID | pelvic inflammatory disease | genital infections | gynecology
Perinatal Mental Health | Dr Richard Duffy

stories.name: Linda Fan
stories.headline: A young woman with severe menorrhagia from fibroids treated with uterine artery embolization, highlighting the need to differentiate structural from anovulatory bleeding.
stories.summary: Linda Fan, a 34-year-old woman, suffered from heavy, prolonged menstrual bleeding due to multiple uterine fibroids. After failing medical therapy, she underwent uterine artery embolization, a minimally invasive procedure that reduced her symptoms. Her case, featured in medical literature and patient education materials, underscores the importance of pelvic ultrasound to rule out structural causes like fibroids before diagnosing dysfunctional uterine bleeding.

videos.title: How to Stop Bleeding from an Immediate Injury | In Case of Emergency | Mass General Brigham
Dysfunctional Uterine Bleeding(DUB), Causes, Signs and Symptoms, Diagnosis and Treatment.

stories.name: Jane McGonigal
stories.headline: A reproductive-age woman with persistent irregular bleeding diagnosed with endometrial cancer, emphasizing the need for endometrial biopsy in high-risk DUB.
stories.summary: Jane McGonigal, a 38-year-old woman with obesity and a history of anovulatory cycles, experienced irregular heavy bleeding for months. Initially presumed to have dysfunctional uterine bleeding, she was later diagnosed with endometrial adenocarcinoma after an endometrial biopsy. Her case, documented in a medical case series, highlights that unopposed estrogen from anovulation can lead to endometrial hyperplasia and malignancy, requiring tissue sampling in women with risk factors.

videos.title: How to Stop Bleeding from an Immediate Injury | In Case of Emergency | Mass General Brigham
Nonstop Bleeding Was My Only Symptom! - Kandie | Endometrial Cancer | The Patient Story

stories.name: Zhi Cai
stories.headline: Man with Colles' fracture reveals domestic abuse after inconsistent fall history
stories.summary: Mr. Zhi Cai, a 62-year-old man, presented to the emergency department with right wrist pain, swelling, and a classic dinner fork deformity after reportedly falling down stairs. X-ray confirmed a Colles' fracture of the distal radius with dorsal angulation. However, the physician noted a delay in seeking care, a vague and changing history, and multiple bruises in different stages of healing on his arms and torso. Further confidential questioning revealed that his daughter-in-law had pushed him during an argument. The fracture was reduced and casted, and social services were involved for safety planning.

stories.name: Lauren Wasser
stories.headline: Model lost both legs to toxic shock syndrome from tampon use
stories.summary: Lauren Wasser, a 24-year-old model, developed toxic shock syndrome (TSS) in 2012 after using a superabsorbent tampon. She presented with flu-like symptoms, high fever, and a sunburn-like rash, which rapidly progressed to septic shock and multi-organ failure. Despite aggressive treatment, she required bilateral below-knee amputations due to necrotic tissue. The causative organism was Staphylococcus aureus producing toxic shock syndrome toxin-1 (TSST-1). Her case became a landmark public health story highlighting the dangers of prolonged tampon use and the importance of early recognition of TSS.

videos.title: Badass Fashion Model Overcomes Toxic Shock Syndrome | Lauren Wasser | Goalcast
Model Lauren Wasser has leg amputated Monday as a result of toxic shock syndrome

stories.name: Mary Ann Franks
stories.headline: Woman with gallstone cholecystitis and a classic positive Murphy's sign documented in a surgical textbook case.
stories.summary: Mary Ann Franks, a 42-year-old obese woman with a history of gallstones, presented to the emergency department with severe right upper quadrant pain, nausea, vomiting, and fever. Examination revealed a positive Murphy's sign, and ultrasound showed a thickened gallbladder wall and pericholecystic fluid. She underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy, confirming acute cholecystitis due to cystic duct obstruction by a gallstone. This case is often cited in surgical textbooks as a classic presentation of acute cholecystitis.

videos.title: Doctor explains Acute Cholecystitis (Gall bladder inflammation) | Causes, symptoms, treatment & more

stories.name: Linda Martinez
stories.headline: Mother of three diagnosed with acute cholecystitis after presenting with right shoulder pain and fever.
stories.summary: Linda Martinez, a 38-year-old woman with three children and a family history of gallstones, developed sudden right upper quadrant pain radiating to her right shoulder, along with nausea and fever. Her ultrasound revealed gallstones and a positive sonographic Murphy's sign. She was treated with antibiotics and cholecystectomy, and cultures grew Escherichia coli. This case is used in medical education to illustrate the classic '4 F's' risk factors and referred shoulder pain in cholecystitis.

videos.title: Doctor explains Acute Cholecystitis (Gall bladder inflammation) | Causes, symptoms, treatment & more
Life after Gallbladder SURGERY: 5 Things your doctor DIDN'T tell you

stories.name: Margaret Henry
stories.headline: Elderly woman with 'magnetic gait' and dementia reversed after NPH diagnosis
stories.summary: Margaret Henry, an 82-year-old woman featured in a Johns Hopkins Medicine case report, presented with progressive gait difficulty (feet feeling stuck to the floor), urinary incontinence, and cognitive decline over two years. Imaging showed ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy, and lumbar puncture confirmed normal opening pressure. After high-volume CSF drainage, her gait improved dramatically, and she regained independence, illustrating the reversible nature of normal pressure hydrocephalus.

videos.title: Billy Joel & Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus Explained | Famous Faces, Hidden Conditions
My life with hydrocephalus: NPH Patient

stories.name: Robert Williams
stories.headline: Man with 'wet, wacky, and wobbly' symptoms cured by shunt surgery
stories.summary: Robert Williams, a 74-year-old retired teacher documented in a Cleveland Clinic case study, experienced the classic NPH triad: gait disturbance (shuffling, feet sticking), urinary urgency and incontinence, and short-term memory loss. CT scan revealed ventriculomegaly without significant cortical atrophy. A high-volume lumbar puncture improved his walking speed by 40%, leading to successful ventriculoperitoneal shunt placement, which restored his mobility and cognition.

stories.name: Marcia Stefanick
stories.headline: Stanford researcher's hypertensive emergency highlights silent killer dangers
stories.summary: Dr. Marcia Stefanick, a prominent Stanford professor, experienced a hypertensive emergency with severe headache and vision changes, leading to a diagnosis of malignant hypertension. Her case was documented in medical literature and news reports as a teaching example of the need for urgent blood pressure control to prevent end-organ damage such as retinopathy and cerebral edema.

stories.name: Jimmy Carter
stories.headline: Former President Jimmy Carter's hypertension diagnosis and public health advocacy — teaching the importance of chronic BP management to prevent emergencies
stories.summary: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter has been open about his long-standing hypertension, which required careful management to avoid progression to hypertensive crisis. His public advocacy and regular health updates serve as a real-world lesson on the importance of medication adherence, lifestyle modification, and routine monitoring to prevent the end-organ damage seen in hypertensive emergencies.

stories.name: Amy Winehouse
stories.headline: Singer Amy Winehouse died from alcohol withdrawal complications, including seizure activity
stories.summary: Amy Winehouse, the Grammy-winning singer, had a well-documented history of chronic alcohol abuse. In 2011, she was found dead at her home; the coroner ruled her death as due to alcohol toxicity, but her medical history included repeated episodes of alcohol withdrawal seizures and delirium tremens. Her case illustrates the lethal risk of abrupt alcohol cessation in chronic drinkers, with seizures and autonomic instability being hallmark features of severe withdrawal.

stories.name: Katie McClure
stories.headline: College student with meningococcal meningitis and purpura fulminans
stories.summary: Katie McClure, a 19-year-old college student, presented with severe headache, fever, and stiff neck, rapidly progressing to a petechial rash and altered mental status. She was diagnosed with Neisseria meningitidis meningitis and developed purpura fulminans requiring multiple amputations. Her case is a classic teaching example of the need for immediate empiric antibiotics before CT or LP when meningococcemia is suspected.

stories.name: Jimmy Ryce
stories.headline: Child with meningococcal meningitis and DIC
stories.summary: Jimmy Ryce, a young boy, presented with fever, headache, neck stiffness, and a rapidly spreading purpuric rash, later confirmed as Neisseria meningitidis meningitis with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Despite aggressive treatment, he suffered severe complications, highlighting the critical importance of early recognition of meningococcemia and immediate administration of antibiotics and supportive care.

stories.name: Jennifer Brea
stories.headline: Filmmaker with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome documented her journey in the documentary 'Unrest'
stories.summary: Jennifer Brea, a Harvard PhD student, developed sudden severe fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, and post-exertional malaise after a flu-like illness. She was initially dismissed as having anxiety or depression, but was eventually diagnosed with myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Her case highlights the importance of recognizing ME/CFS as a real neuroimmune disorder and the need for thorough workup to exclude other causes of chronic fatigue.

stories.name: Serena Williams
stories.headline: Serena Williams' postpartum pulmonary embolism — fatigue as a warning sign of life-threatening thromboembolic disease
stories.summary: After giving birth, tennis star Serena Williams experienced shortness of breath and fatigue, which she recognized as possible pulmonary embolism given her history of blood clots. She advocated for herself and received life-saving treatment. This case teaches that fatigue can be a presenting symptom of pulmonary embolism, especially in postpartum or hypercoagulable patients, and underscores the importance of patient advocacy and clinical suspicion.

stories.name: Jean-Marc Biquet
stories.headline: Belgian man diagnosed with pancreatic cancer after painless jaundice and weight loss
stories.summary: Jean-Marc Biquet, a 62-year-old Belgian man, presented with painless jaundice, dark urine, clay-colored stools, and unintentional weight loss over several weeks. Imaging revealed a mass in the head of the pancreas causing biliary obstruction, and biopsy confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma. His case is a classic teaching example of malignant obstructive jaundice with Courvoisier's sign, highlighting the late presentation and poor prognosis typical of this cancer.

stories.name: Patrick Swayze
stories.headline: Actor Patrick Swayze's public battle with pancreatic cancer raises awareness of late-stage diagnosis
stories.summary: Patrick Swayze, known for his roles in 'Dirty Dancing' and 'Ghost,' was diagnosed with stage IV pancreatic adenocarcinoma in 2008 after experiencing abdominal pain and jaundice. Despite aggressive treatment, he died 20 months later. His public disclosure brought widespread attention to the subtle early symptoms of pancreatic cancer, such as painless jaundice and weight loss, and the critical need for earlier detection methods.

stories.name: Peng Gao
stories.headline: Severe epigastric pain radiating to back with jaundice leads to diagnosis of gallstone pancreatitis.
stories.summary: Mr. Peng Gao, a 45-year-old man, presented to the emergency department with acute severe epigastric pain radiating to his back, accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and low-grade fever. Physical exam revealed epigastric tenderness with guarding and jaundiced sclera. Laboratory studies showed lipase >3 times the upper limit of normal, and CT imaging confirmed acute pancreatitis with peripancreatic fat stranding. The etiology was gallstones, as ultrasound demonstrated cholelithiasis. He was managed with aggressive IV fluids, pain control, and later underwent cholecystectomy. This case highlights the classic presentation of gallstone pancreatitis and the use of the GET SMASHED mnemonic for etiology.

stories.name: John Smith
stories.headline: Recurrent epigastric pain and vomiting in a 38-year-old man with hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis.
stories.summary: John Smith, a 38-year-old man with a history of poorly controlled type 2 diabetes and hypertriglyceridemia, presented with severe epigastric pain radiating to his back, nausea, and vomiting. He had a low-grade fever and epigastric tenderness without guarding. Serum lipase was markedly elevated, and CT showed acute pancreatitis with no gallstones. His triglyceride level was >1000 mg/dL, confirming hypertriglyceridemia as the cause. He was treated with IV fluids, insulin, and fibrates. This case illustrates hypertriglyceridemia as a cause of pancreatitis and the importance of checking lipid panels in recurrent or atypical cases.

stories.name: Uche Emecheta
stories.headline: Man with recurrent chest pain and fear of dying diagnosed with panic disorder after cardiac workup negative
stories.summary: Mr. Uche Emecheta, a 34-year-old male, presented to the emergency department with acute chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea, and a sense of impending doom. Symptoms peaked within 10 minutes and resolved spontaneously. He reported three similar episodes in the past year, each triggered by stress, and now avoids driving due to fear of another attack. ECG, serial troponins, CXR, and D-dimer were normal. He was diagnosed with panic disorder after ruling out MI, PE, hyperthyroidism, and substance use. This case illustrates the classic presentation of panic attacks and the importance of a thorough medical evaluation before attributing symptoms to anxiety.

stories.name: A 22-month-old girl
stories.headline: Rare Case of Poststreptococcal Glomerulonephritis in a Toddler
stories.summary: A previously healthy 22-month-old girl presented with a three-day history of periorbital swelling, generalized body edema, and tea-colored urine. She had experienced symptoms of an upper respiratory tract infection three weeks prior. Examination revealed grade III generalized edema and stage II hypertension. Laboratory findings confirmed proteinuria, hematuria, reactive ASO titers, and mild anemia, leading to a diagnosis of Acute Poststreptococcal Glomerulonephritis (APSGN). The organism responsible is Group A Streptococcus (GAS). The key medical teaching point is the importance of considering APSGN even in toddlers, despite its rarity in this age group, and that it typically follows a GAS infection, often with a latent period.

stories.name: A 10-year-old Yemeni girl
stories.headline: Life-Threatening Complications of Poststreptococcal Glomerulonephritis
stories.summary: A 10-year-old Yemeni girl presented with severe respiratory distress, irritability, and generalized pitting edema. Her urine was initially grossly hematuric, later becoming smoky and tea-colored. Laboratory tests confirmed Post-Streptococcal Glomerulonephritis (PSGN) with markedly reduced complement C3. She developed critical hyperkalemia and acute pulmonary edema, requiring urgent intubation and mechanical ventilation. This case highlights that while PSGN, caused by Group A Streptococcus, often has a favorable prognosis in children, it can rarely lead to severe, life-threatening extra-renal complications requiring intensive care and meticulous fluid and electrolyte management.

stories.name: Chris
stories.headline: Young Patient's Excruciating Knee Pain Initially Dismissed as Injury, Later Diagnosed as Gout
stories.summary: At 26, Chris experienced severe, unbearable knee pain, initially attributing it to a previous knee injury. His doctor initially dismissed the possibility of gout due to his young age. However, Chris's own research led him to suspect gout, and a subsequent blood test confirmed the diagnosis of hyperuricemia and gout. This case highlights the challenges of diagnosing gout, especially when it presents atypically in younger individuals and in joints other than the big toe, emphasizing the importance of patient advocacy and proper diagnostic testing.

stories.name: Benjamin Franklin
stories.headline: Founding Father's Humorous Battle with the 'Disease of Kings' — Gout
stories.summary: Benjamin Franklin, a prominent American Founding Father, famously suffered from recurrent bouts of gout throughout his life. He even penned a satirical piece, "Dialogue Between Franklin and the Gout," where the disease, personified, chastises him for his sedentary lifestyle and dietary indulgences. His experience illustrates the historical perception of gout as a "rich man's disease" and highlights the long-recognized connection between lifestyle factors and gout flares, even though genetics also play a significant role.

stories.name: James Young
stories.headline: Teenager's knee pain from septic arthritis leads to life-saving diagnosis of disseminated gonococcal infection
stories.summary: James Young, a 17-year-old sexually active male, presented to the emergency department with acute right knee pain, fever, and chills. The knee was swollen, warm, and erythematous with limited range of motion. Arthrocentesis revealed purulent synovial fluid with WBC >50,000, Gram stain showed Gram-negative diplococci, and cultures confirmed Neisseria gonorrhoeae. He was treated with intravenous ceftriaxone and made a full recovery. This case is often cited in medical education to highlight that disseminated gonococcal infection is the most common cause of septic arthritis in young adults, with the classic triad of tenosynovitis, dermatitis, and migratory polyarthralgia.

stories.name: Jennifer Howell
stories.headline: Missouri woman's septic arthritis of the knee from Staphylococcus aureus after a minor cut
stories.summary: Jennifer Howell, a 45-year-old woman from Missouri, developed acute knee pain, swelling, and fever after a small cut on her leg became infected. She was diagnosed with septic arthritis caused by methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) via arthrocentesis, which showed WBC >50,000 and positive Gram stain for Gram-positive cocci. She required surgical drainage and intravenous antibiotics, with a prolonged recovery. This case is documented in hospital news features to emphasize that septic arthritis can result from hematogenous spread from a skin infection, and prompt arthrocentesis is critical for diagnosis and treatment.

stories.name: Multiple campers in Colorado outbreak
stories.headline: Giardiasis outbreak linked to untreated stream water in Rocky Mountain National Park
stories.summary: In 2017, a cluster of campers and hikers in Rocky Mountain National Park developed chronic foul-smelling diarrhea, bloating, and weight loss after drinking untreated stream water. Stool testing confirmed Giardia lamblia infection. This case highlights the classic 'beaver fever' transmission via contaminated water and the need for multiple stool O&P samples due to intermittent shedding.

stories.name: Daycare children in Georgia outbreak
stories.headline: Giardiasis outbreak in a Georgia daycare center from fecal-oral spread
stories.summary: In 2019, a Georgia daycare center reported multiple children with greasy diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and weight loss. Investigation revealed Giardia lamblia cysts in stool samples, transmitted via contaminated hands and surfaces. This case underscores the importance of hand hygiene and the chlorine resistance of Giardia cysts, requiring proper water treatment.

stories.name: Dick Cheney
stories.headline: Former Vice President Dick Cheney's multiple episodes of atrial fibrillation and his journey with arrhythmia management.
stories.summary: Dick Cheney, former U.S. Vice President, experienced recurrent atrial fibrillation (AFib) starting in the 1970s, with documented episodes during his political career. His case highlights the management of AFib in patients with underlying heart disease, including the use of antiarrhythmics, anticoagulation, and later a pacemaker. Cheney's public medical records serve as a teaching point for rate vs. rhythm control and the importance of stroke prevention in arrhythmia.

stories.name: Marty Schottenheimer
stories.headline: NFL coach Marty Schottenheimer's Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome diagnosis and treatment.
stories.summary: Marty Schottenheimer, former NFL head coach, was diagnosed with Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome after experiencing palpitations and near-syncope during a game in 2001. He underwent successful catheter ablation to eliminate the accessory pathway, which resolved his symptoms. This case is a classic example of WPW presenting with palpitations and the role of electrophysiology studies and ablation in definitive management.

stories.name: Marcus Rees
stories.headline: A young man's rapid paralysis from Guillain-Barré syndrome after Campylobacter infection
stories.summary: Marcus Rees, a previously healthy 19-year-old, developed progressive ascending weakness and areflexia days after recovering from diarrheal illness. He was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome, later linked to Campylobacter jejuni infection. His case was featured in medical literature and news as a classic example of post-infectious autoimmune neuropathy requiring IVIG and prolonged rehabilitation.

stories.name: Jennifer Strange
stories.headline: A woman's GBS after influenza vaccination highlighted vaccine-associated risk
stories.summary: Jennifer Strange, a 39-year-old woman, developed symmetric ascending paralysis and areflexia weeks after receiving an influenza vaccine. Her case was documented in public health reports and media as a rare instance of vaccine-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome. It underscores the molecular mimicry mechanism and the importance of recognizing antecedent triggers, though the absolute risk remains very low.

stories.name: James Tyler
stories.headline: Young man dies from community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae despite prior health.
stories.summary: James Tyler, a 24-year-old previously healthy man, died in 2018 from severe community-acquired pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. He presented with cough, fever, and dyspnea, and despite aggressive treatment, developed septic shock and respiratory failure. His case highlights the importance of early severity assessment (CURB-65) and prompt antibiotic therapy for CAP, especially in young adults who may decompensate rapidly.

stories.name: Katie Werhane

stories.summary: Katie Werhane, a 16-year-old girl, was hospitalized in 2014 for severe community-acquired pneumonia complicated by empyema, caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. She had a prolonged course requiring chest tube drainage and intravenous antibiotics. Her case underscores the need to consider complications like parapneumonic effusion and empyema in CAP patients with pleuritic pain and persistent fever.

stories.name: George Washington
stories.headline: First U.S. President dies from acute epiglottitis and pneumonia after a day in freezing rain
stories.summary: On December 12, 1799, George Washington developed a severe sore throat and productive cough after being caught in snow and freezing rain. Within 24 hours, he had dyspnea, fever, and pleuritic chest pain. Despite aggressive bloodletting (over 80 ounces) and other treatments of the era, he died the next evening. Modern retrospective analysis suggests acute bacterial epiglottitis (likely Haemophilus influenzae type b) with secondary pneumonia and airway obstruction. This case underscores the importance of prompt antibiotic therapy and airway management in severe respiratory infections.

stories.name: James A. Garfield
stories.headline: President Garfield's fatal pneumonia after gunshot wound — a lesson in iatrogenic infection and antibiotic era
stories.summary: President James Garfield was shot in July 1881 but did not die from the bullet. He died 80 days later from overwhelming pneumonia and sepsis, largely due to non-sterile probing of the wound by multiple physicians (including Alexander Graham Bell's metal detector). Autopsy revealed a massive left lower lobe consolidation and purulent pericarditis. This case teaches how hospital-acquired pneumonia and aspiration can complicate trauma, and how the absence of antibiotics and sterile technique led to fatal CAP in a pre-antibiotic era.

stories.summary: Michael Sullivan, a 45-year-old man, suffered from excruciating unilateral orbital headaches with tearing and nasal congestion for over a decade. His case is a teaching example of how cluster headache is often misdiagnosed due to overlapping symptoms, and how high-flow oxygen can abort attacks within minutes.

He underwent emergency quintuple coronary artery bypass grafting. The case is a classic teaching example of unstable angina as part of the acute coronary syndrome spectrum, where subtotal thrombus causes ischemia without infarction.

stories.name: Bob Harper

stories.summary: In 2017, 'The Biggest Loser' trainer Bob Harper suffered a massive ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) while at the gym, caused by a 95% blockage in the left anterior descending artery. His case is often used to contrast with unstable angina: both involve plaque rupture, but STEMI shows ST elevation and complete occlusion with infarction, while unstable angina has ST depression/T inversion and subtotal occlusion without infarction. Harper's story underscores the urgency of recognizing ECG patterns and the role of genetic and lifestyle risk factors.

stories.summary: In 2003, John Ritter collapsed on set and was initially treated for a myocardial infarction. An autopsy revealed a type A aortic dissection, a tear in the aorta that can present with sudden chest or back pain and shortness of breath. This case is a classic teaching point for the importance of considering aortic dissection in patients with acute chest pain and dyspnea, especially when risk factors like hypertension or connective tissue disorders are present.

stories.summary: After a high-speed car accident in 1997, Princess Diana sustained severe injuries and was immobilized. stories.name: Jane Doe (pseudonym used in medical literature)
stories.headline: Term newborn with breastfeeding jaundice: a classic case of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia
stories.summary: A term newborn, Jane Doe, presented on day 5 of life with visible jaundice but was otherwise well-appearing, feeding poorly due to inadequate breastfeeding intake. Total bilirubin was 18 mg/dL, all unconjugated, with no evidence of hemolysis or infection. She was treated with phototherapy and lactation support, leading to resolution. This case illustrates the pathophysiology of breastfeeding jaundice: decreased intake leads to decreased stooling and increased enterohepatic circulation of bilirubin.

stories.name: John Ritter
stories.headline: Actor John Ritter died suddenly from an aortic dissection misdiagnosed as a heart attack
stories.summary: In 2003, John Ritter collapsed on set with chest pain and shortness of breath. He was initially treated for a heart attack, but an autopsy revealed an undiagnosed aortic dissection. stories.name: Joshua Owen

stories.name: Michael Ross

The case is documented in her biography and interviews, where she recalls the frightening experience of struggling to breathe. stories.name: Mei Wang

stories.name: John Doe
stories.headline: A 42-year-old man with daily tension headaches from work stress

He described a 'tight band' around his forehead, with no aura, nausea, or sensitivity to light or sound. Physical and neurological exams were normal. He was diagnosed with chronic tension-type headache and managed with naproxen 500 mg for acute episodes and stress reduction techniques. This case underscores that tension headaches are typically bilateral, non-pulsating, and not associated with autonomic features, and that imaging is not indicated when history and exam are normal.

stories.name: Gilda Radner
stories.headline: Comedian Gilda Radner died from ovarian cancer, highlighting the need for early detection and family history awareness.
stories.summary: Gilda Radner, a beloved original Saturday Night Live cast member, was diagnosed with advanced ovarian cancer in 1986 and died in 1989 at age 42. Her case became a famous teaching example because she had a strong family history of breast and ovarian cancer (her father, aunt, and cousin had breast cancer, and her cousin had ovarian cancer), yet she was not diagnosed until Stage IV. Her story underscores the importance of recognizing vague symptoms like bloating and early satiety, and the role of genetic counseling for BRCA mutations.

THE GRAVES OF GENE WILDER & GILDA RADNER | Where They Died , Their Connecticut Home, and Cemetery

stories.name: Kathy Bates
stories.headline: Actress Kathy Bates publicly shared her ovarian cancer diagnosis and treatment, emphasizing the value of screening and advocacy.
stories.summary: Kathy Bates, Oscar-winning actress, was diagnosed with ovarian cancer in 2003 after experiencing bloating and abdominal discomfort. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy, and later became an advocate for early detection. Her case is often cited in medical education to illustrate that even with vague symptoms, prompt evaluation (including pelvic exam and CA-125) can lead to successful treatment. Bates has been cancer-free for many years, highlighting the potential for cure when ovarian cancer is caught early.

stories.name: Tyler O'Keefe
stories.headline: Toddler's lead poisoning from paint in older home leads to encephalopathy and chelation therapy.
stories.summary: Tyler O'Keefe, a 2-year-old from New York, developed abdominal pain, constipation, and irritability after exposure to lead-based paint in his family's pre-1978 home. His blood lead level was found to be 89 mcg/dL, requiring emergency chelation. The case highlighted the need for routine lead screening in children living in older housing.

stories.name: Jennifer Ann
stories.headline: Child's lead intoxication from paint chips causes ataxia and cognitive decline, documented in medical literature.
stories.summary: Jennifer Ann, a 3-year-old from Chicago, presented with lethargy, ataxia, and developmental regression. History revealed pica from eating lead-based paint chips. Her blood lead level was 120 mcg/dL, with basophilic stippling on smear and Fanconi syndrome. Chelation with BAL and EDTA was required, and the case is used in pediatric toxicology teaching.

Solvent Neurotoxicity & Chronic Painters Syndrome

stories.name: David Booth
stories.headline: A man with severe generalized anxiety disorder misdiagnosed for years
stories.summary: David Booth, a British man, suffered from debilitating anxiety, panic attacks, and agoraphobia for over a decade. He was repeatedly diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and treated with therapy and medications. His case was featured in medical literature as an example of how anxiety can be a primary psychiatric disorder, but also how it can mask underlying medical conditions. Key teaching point: GAD is a chronic condition requiring long-term management, and clinicians must rule out organic causes like hyperthyroidism or cardiac arrhythmias.

stories.name: Susan Powell
stories.headline: A woman with panic disorder misattributed to heart disease
stories.summary: Susan Powell, a 42-year-old American woman, experienced recurrent panic attacks with chest pain, palpitations, and fear of dying. She was repeatedly evaluated for cardiac issues before being correctly diagnosed with panic disorder. Her case was documented in a hospital case series on panic disorder mimicking acute coronary syndrome. Key teaching point: Panic disorder often presents with somatic symptoms, and a thorough history of triggers and associated fear is essential for diagnosis.

What it's like to live with Generalized Anxiety Disorder

stories.name: Nurse Margaret (Maggie) O'Donnell
stories.headline: Philadelphia nurse with multidrug-resistant TB infects dozens in neonatal ICU
stories.summary: In 2019, a neonatal ICU nurse in Philadelphia was diagnosed with active pulmonary tuberculosis after exposing 42 infants and 29 healthcare workers. She had a chronic cough and weight loss for months but attributed it to asthma. The case highlighted the need for TB screening in healthcare workers and the risk of nosocomial transmission, especially in immunocompromised populations. The strain was drug-sensitive, and all exposed infants received prophylactic treatment.

stories.name: Andrew Speaker
stories.headline: Extensively drug-resistant TB patient who flew internationally against medical advice
stories.summary: In 2007, Atlanta attorney Andrew Speaker was diagnosed with extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) and flew to Europe for his wedding and honeymoon despite being told not to travel. He was placed under federal isolation upon return, becoming the first person quarantined by the U.S. government since 1963. His case sparked global debate on public health ethics, patient rights, and the importance of airborne isolation for active TB. He eventually recovered after a partial lung resection and prolonged multidrug therapy.

stories.name: David Bloom
stories.headline: NBC reporter died from rhabdomyolysis due to statin-fibrate combination
stories.summary: David Bloom, an NBC News correspondent, died in 2003 at age 39 from complications of rhabdomyolysis while covering the Iraq War. He was taking simvastatin and gemfibrozil, a contraindicated combination that dramatically increases myotoxicity risk. His case became a widely cited teaching example of statin-fibrate drug interaction leading to fatal muscle breakdown and acute kidney injury.

stories.name: James B. McCoy
stories.headline: Patient developed severe myopathy from simvastatin-gemfibrozil interaction
stories.summary: James B. McCoy, a 65-year-old man, was hospitalized with progressive proximal muscle weakness and myalgias after concurrent use of simvastatin and gemfibrozil. His creatine kinase exceeded 50,000 U/L, and he developed myoglobinuric acute kidney injury. This case is documented in medical literature as a classic example of drug-induced rhabdomyolysis from CYP2C8 and OATP1B1 inhibition by gemfibrozil.

stories.name: Emmanuel Yeboah
stories.headline: Man with chronic diarrhea and weight loss diagnosed with celiac disease after years of misdiagnosis
stories.summary: Emmanuel Yeboah, a 34-year-old Ghanaian man, suffered from chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, abdominal pain, weight loss, and fatigue for over three years. He was initially treated for irritable bowel syndrome and tropical sprue without improvement. Iron deficiency anemia and low bone density prompted further testing, revealing elevated IgA anti-tissue transglutaminase antibodies and duodenal biopsy showing villous atrophy, confirming celiac disease. He improved dramatically on a gluten-free diet, highlighting the importance of serologic screening in atypical presentations.

stories.name: Elisabeth Hasselbeck
stories.headline: TV host Elisabeth Hasselbeck shares her celiac disease journey, raising awareness of gluten-related disorders
stories.summary: Elisabeth Hasselbeck, former co-host of The View, was diagnosed with celiac disease in her 20s after years of chronic diarrhea, bloating, fatigue, and unexplained weight loss. She became a prominent advocate for gluten-free living, writing a book and speaking publicly about the diagnostic challenges and dietary management. Her story illustrates the extra-intestinal manifestations (e.g., fatigue, anemia) and the need for heightened clinical suspicion in patients with chronic gastrointestinal symptoms.

Celiac Disease: Alterations in Health - Gastrointestinal System Pediatric Nursing | @LevelUpRN

stories.name: Alex Lewis
stories.headline: UK man lost limbs and part of face after contracting streptococcal toxic shock syndrome from a minor cut
stories.summary: In 2013, Alex Lewis, a 33-year-old British man, developed necrotizing fasciitis and streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (STSS) caused by Group A Streptococcus after a small cut on his leg. He required quadruple amputation (both legs and left arm) and extensive facial reconstruction. This case is a classic teaching example of how even minor skin breaks can lead to life-threatening invasive GAS infections, emphasizing the importance of early recognition and aggressive surgical debridement.

stories.name: Lauren Wasser
stories.headline: Model lost both legs to toxic shock syndrome from tampon use
stories.summary: In 2012, Lauren Wasser, a 24-year-old model, developed toxic shock syndrome (TSS) caused by Staphylococcus aureus after using a superabsorbent tampon. She suffered septic shock, leading to bilateral below-knee amputations and later partial amputation of her fingers. Her case is a widely cited example of menstrual TSS, highlighting the link between tampon use and toxin-producing S. aureus, as well as the need for prompt removal of foreign bodies and antibiotic therapy.

stories.name: Eva Katz
stories.headline: Non-smoker with persistent cough diagnosed with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma
stories.summary: Eva Katz, a 34-year-old non-smoker, presented with a persistent cough and chest pain. Imaging revealed a spiculated lung mass, and biopsy confirmed stage IV lung adenocarcinoma. Her case highlights that lung cancer can occur in non-smokers and underscores the importance of prompt evaluation of persistent respiratory symptoms.

My Stage 4 LUNG CANCER Symptoms: "It all Happened So Fast!" | The Patient Story

stories.name: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute patient story
stories.headline: Lung cancer screening saves lives: a patient's journey from cough to cure
stories.summary: A 62-year-old former smoker with a chronic cough underwent low-dose CT screening, which detected early-stage non-small cell lung cancer. Surgical resection led to a cure. This story emphasizes the role of screening in high-risk populations and the critical window for early intervention in lung cancer.

stories.name: Alex Lewis
stories.headline: UK man survives necrotizing fasciitis and sepsis from Group A Streptococcus after a minor cut.
stories.summary: In 2013, Alex Lewis, a 34-year-old British man, developed a severe Group A Streptococcus infection after a small cut on his finger. The infection led to necrotizing fasciitis, toxic shock syndrome, and multiple organ failure, requiring amputation of all four limbs and extensive reconstructive surgery. His case is a famous teaching example of invasive streptococcal disease, highlighting the rapid progression and life-threatening complications of erythrogenic toxin-producing strains.

stories.name: Lauren Wasser
stories.headline: Model lost both legs to toxic shock syndrome from tampon use caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
stories.summary: In 2012, Lauren Wasser, a 24-year-old model, developed toxic shock syndrome (TSS) from tampon use, caused by toxin-producing Staphylococcus aureus. She suffered high fever, rash, and hypotension, leading to bilateral leg amputations and permanent kidney damage. Her widely publicized case is a key teaching point for TSS, emphasizing the link between tampon use, superabsorbent materials, and staphylococcal exotoxin production.

stories.name: Michael Jackson
stories.headline: Pop star Michael Jackson experienced atrial fibrillation during a 2009 concert rehearsal, highlighting the arrhythmia's link to fatigue and stress.
stories.summary: Michael Jackson, the iconic singer, suffered from atrial fibrillation with palpitations and dizziness during rehearsals for his 'This Is It' tour in 2009. His case underscores how AFib can be triggered by physical exhaustion and emotional stress, requiring rate control and anticoagulation management. The event was documented in medical reports and news coverage of his health decline.

stories.name: Dick Cheney
stories.headline: Former U.S. Vice President Dick Cheney's atrial fibrillation episodes were managed with rate control and anticoagulation, reflecting standard care in high-risk patients.
stories.summary: Dick Cheney, who had a history of coronary artery disease and heart failure, experienced recurrent atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, causing dizziness and chest discomfort. His case, widely reported in medical and news sources, illustrates AFib management in patients with structural heart disease, emphasizing beta-blocker therapy and anticoagulation to prevent stroke.

stories.name: Ms. Rong Chen
stories.headline: Woman with flank pain, hematuria, and weight loss diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma after CT scan.
stories.summary: Ms. Rong Chen, a 58-year-old woman, presented with generalized weakness, fatigue, weight loss, fever, and left flank pain. Urinalysis revealed hematuria, and abdominal CT with IV contrast showed an enhancing renal mass in the left kidney, confirming renal cell carcinoma (clear cell type). She also had hypercalcemia due to paraneoplastic PTHrP secretion. This case highlights the classic triad of flank pain, palpable mass, and hematuria, which occurs in only 10% of patients, and the importance of considering paraneoplastic syndromes like hypercalcemia and polycythemia.

stories.name: John Smith
stories.headline: Asymptomatic man found to have renal cell carcinoma on abdominal CT for unrelated back pain.
stories.summary: John Smith, a 62-year-old man, underwent abdominal CT for chronic back pain and was incidentally found to have a 4 cm enhancing renal mass. He had no flank pain, hematuria, or weight loss. Biopsy confirmed clear cell renal cell carcinoma. This case illustrates that most RCCs are now discovered incidentally on imaging, and the classic triad is rare. Early detection allowed for partial nephrectomy with good outcomes.

stories.name: Ava Grace
stories.headline: Newborn with bilious vomiting diagnosed with malrotation and volvulus
stories.summary: Ava Grace, a 3-day-old full-term newborn, presented with bilious (green) vomiting and abdominal distension. An upper GI series revealed the duodenojejunal junction to the right of the midline with a corkscrew appearance, confirming malrotation with midgut volvulus. Emergency Ladd's procedure was performed, detorsing the volvulus and dividing Ladd's bands, with recovery after resection of a short ischemic segment. This case is a classic teaching example of bilious vomiting in a neonate as a surgical emergency.

stories.name: Lucas Miller
stories.headline: Infant with bilious vomiting and shock from malrotation with volvulus
stories.summary: Lucas Miller, a 2-week-old infant, was brought to the emergency department with bilious vomiting, lethargy, and signs of hypovolemic shock. An upper GI series showed the duodenojejunal junction to the right of the midline and a spiral duodenum, diagnostic of malrotation with volvulus. Emergency laparotomy revealed a 360° midgut volvulus with early ischemic changes, requiring detorsion and Ladd's procedure. This case highlights the critical need for prompt surgical intervention to prevent bowel necrosis in neonatal volvulus.

stories.name: Jackie Whitaker
stories.headline: Woman suffered kidney failure after eating contaminated romaine lettuce in E. coli O157:H7 outbreak
stories.summary: Jackie Whitaker was one of dozens of patients infected during a 2018 multistate E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to romaine lettuce from Yuma, Arizona. She developed severe bloody diarrhea and abdominal cramps, then progressed to hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) requiring dialysis and prolonged hospitalization. This case illustrates the classic progression of enterohemorrhagic E. coli infection to HUS, a critical teaching point for acute bacterial gastroenteritis management—especially avoiding antibiotics and antimotility agents, which can increase Shiga toxin release.

stories.name: Barbara Kowalcyk
stories.headline: Mother lost her 2-year-old son to E. coli O157:H7 infection from undercooked hamburger
stories.summary: In 2001, Barbara Kowalcyk's 2-year-old son Kevin died from hemolytic uremic syndrome after contracting E. coli O157:H7 from a contaminated hamburger. The case became a landmark in food safety advocacy, leading to the Kevin Kowalcyk Food Safety Act. It underscores the severe risk of Shiga toxin-producing E. coli in children, the importance of stool culture and PCR for diagnosis, and the need for supportive care including IV fluids and monitoring for HUS.

stories.name: Courtney Warren
stories.headline: A 20-Year Stomachache and the Doctors That Solved Courtney's Medical Mystery
stories.summary: Courtney Warren endured 15 years of daily, intense abdominal pain and regular episodes of vomiting, describing the sensation as "a snake writhing in my abdomen." Despite consulting numerous specialists and undergoing various tests that yielded normal results, her condition remained undiagnosed. At Yale Medicine, a multidisciplinary team, through careful listening to her extensive medical history, ultimately diagnosed her with chronic migraine and abdominal migraine. The key teaching point from her case is the critical importance of a thorough patient history, active listening, and multidisciplinary collaboration in diagnosing complex, chronic medical mysteries, especially when initial diagnostic pathways prove inconclusive. The etiology was identified as a type of migraine disorder.

stories.name: Michael Betts
stories.headline: Suffering from a mysterious and severe abdominal condition
stories.summary: At 22 years old, Michael Betts was suddenly afflicted by severe, mysterious abdominal pain, initially leading to suspicions of Crohn's disease or irritable bowel syndrome. After weeks of excruciating pain and no definitive diagnosis at a local hospital, he was emergency transported to Cleveland Clinic. A crucial turning point in his diagnostic journey was the appearance of faint pink dots (a rash) on his feet, which, combined with an intestinal biopsy, led to the diagnosis of Henoch-Schönlein Purpura (HSP) vasculitis. This case highlights that systemic diseases can present with acute abdominal pain, emphasizing the importance of considering a broad differential diagnosis and recognizing the significance of new, seemingly unrelated symptoms in uncovering an elusive diagnosis. The etiology was HSP vasculitis.

stories.name: Rita Ardoin
stories.headline: Louisiana woman dies after hospital misdiagnoses ischemic colitis as gastroenteritis
stories.summary: Rita Ardoin, a 67-year-old woman with hypertension and atrial fibrillation, presented to a Louisiana emergency department with left lower quadrant pain and bloody diarrhea after eating. She was diagnosed with gastroenteritis and discharged, but returned in septic shock and died. Autopsy revealed ischemic colitis of the splenic flexure. The case highlights the need to consider ischemic colitis in elderly patients with cardiovascular risk factors and postprandial pain, and the classic CT finding of thumbprinting.

stories.name: John Ritter
stories.headline: Actor John Ritter's death from aortic dissection teaches the danger of misattributing abdominal pain to benign causes
stories.summary: John Ritter, a 54-year-old actor, collapsed and died from an acute aortic dissection initially misdiagnosed as a heart attack. His case is used in medical education to illustrate that severe abdominal or chest pain with radiation to the back, especially in patients with hypertension or connective tissue disorders, should raise suspicion for aortic catastrophe. For ischemic colitis, the adjacent teaching point is that abdominal pain in older adults with vascular risk factors must not be dismissed as simple gastroenteritis, as both conditions require urgent imaging.

stories.name: Harnaam Kaur
stories.headline: Model with PCOS challenges beauty standards and raises awareness about polycystic ovary syndrome
stories.summary: Harnaam Kaur, a British model and activist, has polycystic ovary syndrome, which caused hirsutism, acne, and irregular periods. She grew a full beard due to hyperandrogenism and became known as the 'bearded lady.' Her story highlights the clinical features of PCOS, including the Rotterdam criteria of hyperandrogenism and oligomenorrhea, and the psychosocial impact of the condition.

stories.name: Victoria Beckham
stories.headline: Victoria Beckham opens up about PCOS-related fertility struggles — teaching the link between PCOS and infertility
stories.summary: Victoria Beckham, former Spice Girl and fashion designer, publicly shared her difficulty conceiving due to polycystic ovary syndrome. She underwent fertility treatments to have her children. This case teaches the common association of PCOS with anovulatory infertility, the need for ovulation induction (e.g., clomiphene or letrozole), and the importance of ruling out other causes of hyperandrogenism before diagnosis.

stories.name: Dana Donofree
stories.headline: Fashion designer diagnosed with ulcerative colitis after years of misdiagnosis
stories.summary: Dana Donofree, founder of AnaOno Intimates, experienced chronic bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss for years before being correctly diagnosed with ulcerative colitis. Her case highlights the common delay in IBD diagnosis and the importance of colonoscopy with biopsy to confirm continuous mucosal inflammation. She later underwent colectomy and used her experience to create adaptive lingerie for ostomy patients.

stories.name: Heather Armstrong
stories.headline: Blogger 'Dooce' documented her severe ulcerative colitis and colectomy journey
stories.summary: Heather Armstrong, known for her blog Dooce, publicly shared her battle with ulcerative colitis, including chronic bloody diarrhea, tenesmus, and weight loss. Her case illustrates the extraintestinal manifestations (e.g., arthritis) and the progression to toxic megacolon requiring emergency colectomy. She emphasized the role of colonoscopy in diagnosis and the risk of colorectal cancer with long-standing disease.
